reference: GNU coreutils ptx selected from PATH under system Bash in the C locale; the runner compares raw stdout and the fixture tree.
coverage: GNU and traditional (-G) modes: sentence and line contexts, word definitions and default formats.
Field fitting with -w and -g, head/tail wrapping and the -F truncation flag.
-i/-o word lists, -f folding, -W/-S Emacs regexps and -b break files.
exclusions: Equal keywords from different input files of different sizes: GNU orders them by the addresses of its file buffers, which follow the heap layout; bash-os uses file order. The several-input case uses inputs for which GNU's order is file order.
Locale-specific quoting, multibyte words and very large inputs are not exercised.

cases.purpose: GNU mode: sentence contexts across a line break, default width 72 and gap 3.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat
on the mat
' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.
A second paragraph line	with a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.
' > long
ptx t
ptx long

cases.purpose: Fitting the fields to -w 40/100 and -g 1, with wrapped head and tail fields.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat\non the mat\n' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.\nA second paragraph line\twith a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.\n' > long
ptx -w 40 long
ptx -w 100 long
ptx -g 1 long
ptx -w 30 -g 5 long

cases.purpose: -F sets the truncation flag; an empty -F turns flagging off.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat
on the mat
' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.
A second paragraph line	with a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.
' > long
ptx -F ... -w 50 long
ptx -F '' -w 50 long

cases.purpose: -O roff (quotes doubled) and -T TeX (special characters escaped, key and after split) output, with -M.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat\non the mat\n' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.\nA second paragraph line\twith a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.\n' > long
ptx -O long
ptx -T long
ptx -M yy -O t
ptx -G -T long

cases.purpose: -G: lines are contexts, a word is any run of non-blanks, roff output by default.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat\non the mat\n' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.\nA second paragraph line\twith a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.\n' > long
ptx -G t
ptx -G long
ptx -G -w 50 long

cases.purpose: -G INPUT OUTPUT writes the index to the file OUTPUT; an OUTPUT of - is a file named -, as in GNU.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat\non the mat\n' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.\nA second paragraph line\twith a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.\n' > long
ptx -G t out
/usr/bin/cat out
ptx -G t -
/usr/bin/cat ./-

cases.purpose: -A FILE:LINE references on the left and, with -R, on the right.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat\non the mat\n' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.\nA second paragraph line\twith a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.\n' > long
ptx -A t
ptx -A -R t
ptx -A -R -w 60 long
ptx -T -M zz -A t

cases.purpose: -r: the first field of each line is its reference and lines are contexts.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat
on the mat
' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.
A second paragraph line	with a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.
' > long
printf 'r1 the cat sat
r22 on the mat
' > r
ptx -r r
ptx -r -w 50 r

printf 'the cat sat
on the mat
' > t

cases.purpose: -W word and -S sentence regexps (Emacs syntax), an empty -S, and a -b break file.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat\non the mat\n' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.\nA second paragraph line\twith a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.\n' > long
printf ' .,' > brk
ptx -W '[a-z]+' long
ptx -S '\.' long
ptx -S '' long
ptx -b brk long

' > t

cases.purpose: Bad options and values: usage errors with status 1.
cases.script:
printf 'the cat sat\non the mat\n' > t
printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. It was "very" quick!  Then {it} ran_away & hid $5 #1 50%%.\nA second paragraph line\twith a tab, and some more words to wrap around the width limit of seventy-two columns.\n' > long
st() { if "$@" 2>&1; then echo rc=0; else echo rc=$?; fi; }
st ptx --bogus
st ptx -Z
st ptx -w
st ptx -w x t
st ptx -w 0 t
st ptx -g 0 t
st ptx -G t t2 t3
st ptx --format=x t > fmt
/usr/bin/head -n 1 fmt
/usr/bin/rm fmt
